جُرْنٌ A hollowed stone, [or stone basin,] from which the [ablution termed] وُضُوْء is performed; (K;) water being poured into it; called by the people of El-Medeeneh مهرس [app. مِهْرَس, perhaps a dial. var. of مِهْرَاسٌ, or a mistranscription for this]: so in the M: in the Jm, the مِهْرَاس with which the وضوء is performed. (TA.) ―
-b2- See also جُبٌّ. ―
-b3- [In the present day, applied also to A stone mortar in which things are pounded.] ―
-b4- See also جَرِينٌ, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
